html:
The Chiquitano are an Indigenous people of the Chiquitania, the dry forest and savanna of eastern Bolivia in Santa Cruz department, with a few communities in Brazil. They are the largest lowland Indigenous people of Bolivia.

Their name comes from the Spanish chiquitos, "little ones", said to be for the low doors of their houses. Before Europeans came they were many separate groups speaking different languages. From 1691 the Jesuits gathered them into ten mission towns, the Missions of Chiquitos, where Chiquitano became the common language. The people built large wooden baroque churches and played European music on violins and organs they made themselves.

The Jesuit missions ended in 1767, but six of the churches survive as a World Heritage Site, and music from the mission archives is played at a festival there today. Their neighbours include the Guarayo and Ayoreo.
sum: The Chiquitano are an Indigenous people of the Chiquitania, the dry forest and savanna of eastern Bolivia in Santa Cruz department, with a few communities in Brazil. They are the largest lowland Indigenous people of Bolivia.
